message: German radio message transmitted 27 November 1918 (Childs, p. 217; RICHI-170)

claim.novelty: unconfirmed: the post says 'to my knowledge' unsolved, and no custodian has marked it solved

ciphertext_source.held_by: J. Rives Childs, The History and Principles of German Military Ciphers 1914-1918, p. 217
ciphertext_source.note: transcribed by eye from the page scan in the post; see README caveats

key.keyword_source: Childs pp. 214-215; documented as in use from 9 December 1918, twelve days after this message's date
key.square_note: the scan carries handwritten corrections. Two cells were read wrong on our first pass and the German fixed them: row G column F is the digit 0, row X column A is the letter O (Childs underlines one of the pair). The cell read here as 4 (row A, column X) is the one HMS Canterbury's log settles; its partner cell (row F, column F) then takes 8.

reading: Ein englischer Kreuzer einlieg(end) Sewastopol [2]4sten. Ein Geschwader der Alliierten folgt 26sten.
english: An English cruiser docked at Sevastopol on the 24th. An allied squadron follows on the 26th.
external_corroboration: HMS Canterbury's log places the ship at Sevastopol on 24 November 1918, with an allied squadron on the 26th (cited in the post).
